verdict: both defensible (curator's per-experiment split is the compilation convention; agent's envelope is the paper's own headline line)
evidence: Main-text Fig. 3 (p.4) draws ONE green 'Stochastic' line = the union of three corrected constraints (CASPEr-ZULF comagnetometer, nEDM, CASPEr-ZULF sidebands) plus the K-3He new-force line; Supplementary Fig. 3 (p.10) shows them separately: comagnetometer boundary at log10 g_aNN ~ -3.2 (flat over 1e-21..1e-17 eV, rising to -2.5 at 1e-22), nEDM at -4 to -4.7 over the same masses. The curator's file CASPEr_Comagnetometer.txt (header: 'corrected constraint in 1905.13650', 'g_an/2m_n [GeV^-1]') holds only the comagnetometer piece: flat 6.0e-4 GeV^-1 over 1e-20..1e-18 eV. The agent traced the main-text envelope, so over 1e-21..1e-17 its curve is the nEDM floor (g_an ~ 4e-5 after x2m_n) = 1.0-1.4 dex below the comag curve, and it continues to 7e-14 eV along the sidebands line (GT ends at 1.5e-17). Residual 1.39 dex is the nEDM-vs-comag gap, not a digitisation error: the agent's own points reproduce the green line (e.g. 4e-5 at 1e-19 eV = 10^-4.7 GeV^-1 x 1.88).
policy_question: When a re-analysis paper publishes one envelope over several corrected experiments, does the compilation want the envelope or the per-experiment component (the curator stores per-experiment files: CASPEr_Comagnetometer.txt, nEDM.txt both 'taken from corrected constraint in 1905.13650')?
notes: Agent's notes explicitly describe the curve as the combination of the three corrected limits, so it saw the alternative but did not split. SECONDARY REFERENCE DEFECT: the upstream file stores g_an/2m_n [GeV^-1] and PlotFuncs.py Comagnetometer() multiplies by 2*m_n at plot time; the bench ingested the raw column, so the bench GT is 0.27 dex (factor 1.88) below the canonical g_an. Even a perfect comagnetometer trace with the task-card 2m_N rule would score ~0.27 dex against this GT. My residual estimate agent-vs-true-comag: ~1.45 dex; agent-vs-nEDM component: ~0.1 dex.

verdict: agent right (paper's own Fig. 5 supports the agent's curve in both arXiv versions); curator's file is a different paper's re-derivation
evidence: Fig. 5 (p.4, both v1 and the Apr-2018 published version) shows the MICROSCOPE |d_e| line flat at ~2.3e-4 (one third of a decade above the 1e-4 gridline), rising near 1e-12 eV and reaching |d_e|=1 at ~2e-11 eV; text: 'exclude a new region above |d_e| = 1e-4 for 1e-18 < m < 1e-11 eV'. Agent: flat 2.34e-4, exits at 2.2e-11 eV, i.e. a faithful trace. Curator file ScalarPhoton/MICROSCOPE.txt (header cites 1712.00483): flat 1.08e-4, rising from 3e-13 eV and reaching 1.6 at 4e-12 eV, a factor 2.2 lower and a factor ~5 lower in cutoff mass than anything in this paper. That file instead matches the 'MICROSCOPE Ti/Pt' curve of Hees et al. 2018 (1807.04512, Fig. 3 top): agent's trace of that curve (flat 9.9e-5, exits at 6.4e-12 eV) agrees with the curator file to 0.03-0.13 dex over 1e-16..3e-12 eV. Scorer: forward median 0.32 dex = 0.34 dex on the flat part plus a 0.8-2.1 dex tail from the cutoff-mass offset.
notes: Not a version issue (v1 and published Fig. 5 are the same curve to the eye). The curator file is a legitimate MICROSCOPE bound but derived by a later paper with a different Earth-model treatment; against this paper's own figure the agent's residual would be <0.1 dex. Agent notes do not discuss the alternative (no reason to). Scalar d_me file for the same paper (ScalarElectron/MICROSCOPE.txt) has the same mass profile, consistent with both files coming from Hees et al. rather than from 1712.00483, which gives no d_me bound at all.

verdict: both defensible; multi-coupling paper (scalars to electrons/nucleons, dark photon, Higgs portal); agent chose the new SN1987A dark-photon bound, the benchmark holds only the red-giant scalar files for this paper

verdict: both defensible; curator took the normal-CCSN (1 B) contour, agent the low-energy-SN (0.1 B) contour; the paper shows both with equal standing

verdict: both defensible; agent returned the union envelope of all the paper's cosmological regions (Fig. 1), the compilation splits them into per-constraint files (EBL, XRAY, x_ion, ...) and the bench graded against x_ion.txt
evidence: Fig. 1 of Cadamuro & Redondo is a summary plot with many separately labelled cosmological regions (Optical/EBL, X-rays, x_ion, DM, CMB y/mu, N_eff, D, 4He, EM/hadronic showers). Agent (59 pts, 4.6 eV..1e11 eV): explicitly 'the union of the paper's own cosmology regions', clamped at the figure floor 1e-18 and top 1e-4. papers.json lists three curator files for this paper: EBL.txt (305 eV..7.8e10 eV), XRAY.txt (387 eV..5e6 eV), x_ion.txt (27..417 eV); the scorer picked x_ion.txt (best match): over 27-417 eV the agent's envelope follows the x_ion lower edge only partly (residual 0.44 median, p90 5.2 dex because the envelope drops to the 1e-18 floor above 154 eV where the DM-overclosure region takes over).

verdict: curator's choice is the one literally in the canonical plane (Fig. 4b, coupling only to photons); agent recast the hypercharge-coupling limit (Fig. 4a) via g_agamma = g_aBB cos^2(theta_W), a model-dependent projection that is ~1 dex stronger
evidence: Figure 4 (p.6-7): left panel 'Limits on a coupling to two hypercharge bosons' (axis Log10 g_aBB), right panel 'Limits on a coupling only to photons' (axis Log10 g_agamma); text: 'To obtain the limits in this case we have simply rescaled the limits with the appropriate lower ALP production cross section' (photon-only production is off-shell, hence weaker). Curator LEP.txt: plateau 6.5e-3 GeV^-1 for 0.2-10 GeV, 8-9e-4 above 10 GeV = right panel. Agent: 5.5e-4 plateau and 1.7e-4 above 10 GeV = left panel x0.769, i.e. 1.07 and 0.7 dex below. policy_question: Whether a limit derived for a hypercharge coupling (which also induces aZgamma/aZZ couplings that drive the Z->a gamma production) may be reported in the g_agamma plane by multiplying by cos^2(theta_W), or whether only the photon-only scenario belongs there.

verdict: both defensible; agent reported the NFW-profile conservative bound the abstract headlines, curator stored the ancillary file's max-D-factor (optimistic, generalized-Hernquist) column

E-print ancillary gagg_line.txt has three columns: mass, 'photon coupling (max D-factor)' (median 9.26e-12) and '(min D-factor)' (median 1.24e-10), both generalized-Hernquist. verdict: both defensible; title 'Axion and dark photon limits from Crab Nebula': agent reported the ALP-photon exclusion (Fig. 3), the compilation holds only the dark-photon curve (Crab_2.txt) for this paper

verdict: agent right on inspection (minimum 1.50e-9 at 2.035 neV = paper's quoted limit); curator's 2-vertex flat line vs the agent's resonance-shaped curve evaluated at the line's endpoints

verdict: agent right for the paper as it exists today (v2, Mar 2023); curator's file matches the superseded v1 curve (rho_DM = 0.4, earlier analysis), ~0.3 dex stronger

verdict: agent right on inspection (minimum 5.5e-11 vs paper's 6.86e-11 and GT 6.9e-11); both sides are coarse samplings (95 vs 74 points) of an extremely spiky curve, so pointwise residuals alias the spikes

verdict: both defensible; agent reported the headline Cas A bound (Eq. 37, eps m < 1.5e-8 MeV), curator's file follows the stronger NS1987A region (Eq. 39, eps m < 3e-9 MeV) although its header says 'Cas A cooling'

verdict: undecided between POL and REF: the paper's Fig. 1 shows two ORGAN dark-photon curves (opaque 'fixed polarisation' ~1-2e-12 and transparent 'random polarisation' ~5e-13); the agent traced the opaque one, the curator's Rescaled/ORGAN-1a.txt (header 'rescaled to fixed polarisation scenario') coincides with the lower one

verdict: both defensible; the paper re-derives several linear-coupling EP curves ('summarize existing results'), the agent reported the MICROSCOPE Ti/Pt one, the compilation files the Eot-Wash Be/Ti one under this paper (and files the MICROSCOPE one under 1712.00483)

verdict: curator right; agent returned the per-bin minimum (lower envelope) of a spiky limit, which overstates the bound wherever sensitivity is lost at DD-sequence harmonics

verdict: both defensible; agent traced the upper envelope of the jagged Yb+/Sr 95% CL spectrum, which is the boundary of the grey excluded region drawn in Fig. 6; curator stored the raw jagged spectrum with its deep downward spikes

verdict: agent right in plane; the benchmark's only GT for this review is a B-L recast of a Casimir compilation from a different paper (2009.04517), so no curve from quant-ph/0106045 exists to grade against

verdict: curator right (follows the paper's drawn exclusion boundary = upper edge of the noisy band); agent reported the geometric centre of the band, 0.30 dex low; borderline case exactly at the cut

verdict: both defensible on the band; curator additionally applied a x2 B->B-L charge rescale that the agent omitted (secondary conversion gap)
evidence: Fig. 5 (semi_full_all_upper_limits.png): 95% CL eps^2 vs mass, fully-coherent limit is a jagged band ~1 decade wide in eps^2 at 1e-19..4e-18 eV (red) widening to 4-5 decades at 1e-15..1e-14 eV (black); caption/text: 'coupling of dark photons to baryons in the test masses'. Curator file LISAPathfinder.txt header: 'Rescaled by factor 2 for B-L coupling rather than B', values = band upper envelope (in eps) x2; bench then multiplies by e. Agent: g = e*sqrt(eps^2) at the band's per-bin median, no factor 2. Predicted offset: 0.3 (factor 2) + 0.25 (half of a 0.5-dex band in eps) = 0.55 dex at low mass, 0.3 + ~1.0 at high mass; observed: 0.6 dex at 1e-19 eV rising to 1.0 dex at 1e-15 eV (scorer median 0.90, p90 1.97).
policy_question: How to reduce a 1-5-decade-wide jagged 95% band to one curve (upper envelope vs median), and whether a baryon-coupling limit belongs in the B-L plane with a charge rescale.
notes: Agent notes flag both issues themselves ('a digitisation following the band's lower or upper envelope could differ by more than a factor of 2 in g at m > 3e-16 eV'; 'other charge assignment implicit'). The factor-2 recast is the curator's, not the paper's.

verdict: curator right under the task card's rule; the paper derives its own updated MICROSCOPE B-L bound (Appendix E), which the agent classified as a comparison-only reinterpretation and returned no points
evidence: p.5: 'in Appendix E, we derive an updated limit on the gauge coupling of a new, long-range B-L coupled fifth force given the latest MICROSCOPE results'; Fig. 5 caption: 'For MICROSCOPE, we show the bound based on the first and final results, the latter of which we compute in Appendix E'. Curator VectorB-L/MICROSCOPE.txt header: 'MICROSCOPE EP violation limit ... Updated in https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.02381' (1001 pts, 1e-30..1e-12 eV, 7e-26..7e-19). Agent: is_projection = true, data_points = [], notes: 'The Eot-Wash and MICROSCOPE curves in Fig. 5 (and the epsilon_B-L recast in Appendix E) are reinterpretations of other experiments' published results, shown for comparison, not a new measured limit'.

verdict: both defensible; agent took the strongest (blue, T_osc optimised) of three nested excluded regions, curator the green 'most conservative' one; both are faithful traces
evidence: Fig. 1 (plots/ma_fa.pdf): three nested regions, green 'T_osc = 1 keV' (conservative), red 'T_osc = 1 keV, PL', blue 'T_osc ~ sqrt(m_a M_pl)' (largest). Curator Axinovae.txt header: 'green line in fig.1 - most conservative estimate'; its 11 points (1.1e-20, 3.4e-17) -> (6.5e-14, 1e-7) follow the steep green boundary. miss_criterion_observed: forward median residual >= 0.30 dex, or no comparable GT curve for the agent's coupling type, or no points
notes: 2212.01971 recorded as POL but undecided between POL and REF (two candidates given in its entry).

2 secondary reference defects noted inside entries that were filed under another primary cause: 1905.13650 (bench GT lacks the 2*m_n factor PlotFuncs applies at plot time, 0.27 dex) and 2301.08736 (curator x2 B->B-L recast).
Of the 9 no_comparable_gt/no_points papers the scorer already accepts the agent type as correct for 8; those misses are coverage/attribution issues (POL or REF), not ID.
